providers.name: Jira

sub_criteria.note: No first-party JS/TS SDK — [`jira.js`](https://github.com/MrRefactoring/jira.js) is community
ADF (Atlassian Document Format) for rich text — proprietary JSON tree; [JRACLOUD-77436](https://jira.atlassian.com/browse/JRACLOUD-77436) (Markdown API) still unresolved

schema_flexibility.justification: Unlimited typed custom fields with dynamic schema — [Fields API](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issue-fields/). Soft guidance ≤ 1,000 fields/instance for performance; no hard cap.

rate_limits.justification: [65,000 points/hour per site](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rate-limiting/). Bulk endpoints push effective throughput higher (50 issues per bulk-create, 1,000 IDs per bulk-edit).

real_time.justification: 30+ [webhook event identifiers](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/webhooks/) covering issues, comments, worklogs, sprints, projects, users, versions, attachments. Retry semantics documented.

sub_criteria.note: OAuth app registration requires Atlassian developer console + scope config

data_portability.justification: Full API coverage + bulk endpoints. No single "export everything" endpoint; admin CSV/JSON export exists via console but is not API-first.

sub_criteria.note: Rovo agents assignable as Jira assignees (beta Feb 2026)
Atlassian-led Claude / Rovo integration + published Rovo case studies

providers.bottom_line: Jira leads overall — 2025's MCP + Rovo rollout flipped its historically weakest dimension into its strongest. ADF and no first-party SDK remain real papercuts.
providers.gotcha: ADF description format still mandatory on v3 — requires converter

providers.name: GitHub

sub_criteria.note: 8/14 native (priority, due_date, start_date, estimated_hours, logged_hours all require ProjectsV2 custom fields; issue `state` is binary not full status)
No ops gaps — issues moveable across projects
Dual model — REST for Issues, GraphQL-only for ProjectsV2
[Octokit](https://github.com/octokit) — first-party JS/TS, Ruby, Go, .NET (no official Python; PyGithub is community)

schema_flexibility.justification: ProjectsV2 supports 5 typed field types (text, number, date, single-select, iteration) with 50-option cap on single-select; no `updateProjectV2Field` mutation (option edits are delete+recreate = data loss). Custom fields are project-scoped, not issue-scoped. [Understanding fields](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/understanding-fields)

rate_limits.formula: REST 5,000/hr = 83 rpm; GraphQL 5,000 pts/hr × 10 aliases = 833 ops/min
rate_limits.justification: [REST PAT: 5,000/hr](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api); [GraphQL: 5,000 points/hr](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/overview/rate-limits-and-node-limits-for-the-graphql-api). With GraphQL aliased multi-mutation, effective throughput ≈ 830 ops/min (83 req/min × 10 typical aliases). Enterprise Cloud raises to 10,000–15,000/hr.

data_portability.justification: Full API + Git-native storage (inherently portable) + documented [migration tooling](https://docs.github.com/en/migrations).

sub_criteria.note: [github/github-mcp-server](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server) — v1.0.0 GA 2026-04-16, issues + projects + repo surface
Copilot coding agent [GA 2025-09-25](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-25-copilot-coding-agent-is-now-generally-available/) — assignable to issues

providers.bottom_line: GitHub holds 4.4. Strong everywhere except schema flex, with the dual Issues/ProjectsV2 model as its enduring ergonomic cost.
providers.gotcha: Dual model (Issues REST + ProjectsV2 GraphQL) multiplies API surface

providers.name: Linear

sub_criteria.note: 11/14 native (78.5% — just under 80%; `start_date` is read-only `startedAt`, `estimated_hours` is unitless points, `logged_hours` missing)

schema_flexibility.justification: No arbitrary user-defined custom fields. Extensibility = labels, projects, cycles, and (June 2025) [Asks fields](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-06-05-asks-fields-and-triage-routing) scoped to triage — not general-purpose.

rate_limits.justification: [5,000 req/hr + 3M complexity pts/hr](https://linear.app/developers/rate-limiting) on API keys; 10,000 pts max per query. At 10-alias typical batch → effective ~830 ops/min. Complexity budget lets denser queries fetch hundreds of items per request.

real_time.justification: 14 entity types × 3 action types + specialized (Issue SLA, OAuthApp revoked, **Agent session events**) = 40+ [webhook events](https://linear.app/developers/webhooks).

data_portability.justification: Full GraphQL coverage — everything is fetchable via paged queries. No dedicated bulk-export endpoint.

sub_criteria.note: [Linear MCP server](https://linear.app/docs/mcp) — hosted, find/create/update for issues/projects/comments
[Agent Sessions API](https://linear.app/developers/agents) — agents as first-class users with session lifecycle
Published case studies (Rivet May 2025, Reflag) + webhook event category for agents

providers.bottom_line: Linear remains the DX leader and has the most mature agent primitives (sessions, actor-based auth). Lack of custom fields is the only real weakness.
providers.gotcha: Hard ceiling on custom fields (labels + Asks only); estimate is points, not hours

providers.name: Monday.com

sub_criteria.note: 5/14 native (id, title, parent_id, created_at, updated_at); all other fields require column-type custom fields
Text / long-text column types in standard formats

schema_flexibility.justification: Fully dynamic schema — 27+ [column types](https://developer.monday.com/api-reference/reference/column-types-reference) including status, dropdown, text, long_text, numbers, date, timeline, people, tags, checkbox, link, email, phone, rating, color_picker, dependency, file, formula, mirror, connect_boards, subitems, time_tracking, hour, location, vote, world_clock, country. No hard cap on columns per board.

rate_limits.formula: Personal token 1M pts/min on Free ÷ 1 pt/op (GET) = 1,000,000 ops/min
rate_limits.justification: Personal token [10M complexity pts/min](https://developer.monday.com/api-reference/docs/rate-limits) (1M Free/Trial). `create_item` ≈ 10k pts → ≈ 1,000 writes/min; reads far more. Daily call caps apply at low tiers but complexity is the binding constraint for integrations.

real_time.justification: ~15+ [webhook events](https://developer.monday.com/api-reference/reference/webhooks) including `change_column_value`, `change_status_column_value`, `create_item`, `create_subitem`, `item_archived/deleted/moved`, `create_update`, plus 12 app-lifecycle events. Board-scoped registration.

sub_criteria.note: No service-account / SSO-integrated token for enterprise (OAuth-only path)

data_portability.justification: Full GraphQL API. No dedicated bulk export; board-based model requires per-board schema introspection before extraction.

sub_criteria.note: [Sidekick](https://monday.com/w/mcp), Vibe, AI Blocks — programmable AI surface
Hosted MCP integrations with Claude / Cursor / Copilot

providers.bottom_line: Dynamic column schema that penalized completeness is precisely what makes flexibility and rate limits excellent. First-party MCP closes the AI gap.
providers.gotcha: Dynamic column schema — adapter must introspect each board before mapping

providers.name: Asana

sub_criteria.note: 11/14 native (status requires custom field; native priority exists but limited to 3 fixed values)
Batch API exists but per-request limits apply
[`asana` on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/asana) + [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/asana/) — first-party, active (Node/Python); Java/PHP/Ruby deprecated

schema_flexibility.justification: Typed custom fields: text, number, date, single-select, multi-select, people, formula (read-only). [100 fields/project](https://developers.asana.com/docs/custom-fields-guide) (raised from 30). Workspace-scoped.

rate_limits.formula: 150 rpm on Free tier (Paid tier would score band 5 at 1,500 rpm)
rate_limits.justification: [Free: 150 req/min; Paid: 1,500 req/min](https://developers.asana.com/docs/rate-limits). Score at Free = band 3 (Paid would be band 5). Search capped at 60/min. Duplication jobs capped at 5 concurrent.

real_time.justification: Resource-level [webhooks](https://developers.asana.com/docs/webhooks-guide) with HMAC signing, exponential-backoff retry, 24h failure expiry. Compact events (re-fetch required). ~15+ event combinations.

data_portability.justification: Full API + batch + CSV export (UI). Tasks-in-multiple-projects adds extraction complexity but is tractable.

sub_criteria.note: [Asana MCP Server V2](https://developers.asana.com/docs/mcp-server) — GA Feb 2026, streamable HTTP, ~42 tools (V1 SSE server sunset 2026-05-11)
AI Studio / Asana Intelligence has no public API

providers.bottom_line: Asana's MCP V2 + Service Accounts raise the floor considerably. AI Studio being product-only rather than programmable is the remaining gap.
providers.gotcha: Native priority limited to 3 fixed values; rich status still needs a custom field

providers.name: ClickUp

sub_criteria.note: REST v2 stable, v3 endpoints [shipping gradually](https://developer.clickup.com/) (dual version adds minor confusion)

schema_flexibility.justification: ~18 [custom field types](https://developer.clickup.com/docs/customfields) (text, number, currency, date, checkbox, email, phone, URL, dropdown, labels, rating, progress, people, tasks, location, emoji, formula, files). 500 options per dropdown/label. Free tier capped at 60 total field uses; paid unlimited.

rate_limits.formula: 100 rpm at entry tiers (Business Plus 1,000 rpm would score band 5; Enterprise 10,000 rpm)
rate_limits.justification: [Per-token, per-minute](https://developer.clickup.com/docs/rate-limits): Free/Unlimited/Business = **100 rpm**, Business Plus = 1,000, Enterprise = 10,000. Score at Free = band 2. Business Plus would be band 5.

real_time.justification: Comprehensive [webhooks](https://developer.clickup.com/docs/webhooks) — task / list / folder / space / goal / keyResult × create/update/delete plus `*` wildcard. ~20+ events.

data_portability.justification: Full API coverage. No bulk-export endpoint. 5-level hierarchy (Workspace → Space → Folder → List → Task → Subtask) means extraction requires walking the tree.

sub_criteria.note: [Official ClickUp MCP server](https://developer.clickup.com/docs/connect-an-ai-assistant-to-clickups-mcp-server) (OAuth-only, task CRUD + Brain context)
2026 roadmap for external MCP tool integration

providers.bottom_line: Completeness leader (14/14 native) with MCP and Super Agents closing the AI gap. Free-tier rate limit and no first-party SDK are the drag.
providers.gotcha: Free/Unlimited/Business = 100 rpm; realistic sync needs Business Plus (1k rpm)

providers.name: Todoist

sub_criteria.note: 9/14 native (no status beyond `is_completed`/`checked`; no `start_date`; no `logged_hours`; `updated_at` not consistently exposed)
`move_task` command — historical "can't move between projects" gotcha is fixed
Single unified v1 model (REST v2 + Sync v9 deprecating early 2026)

schema_flexibility.justification: Labels only — no user-defined custom fields.

rate_limits.justification: [1,000 req / 15 min REST](https://developer.todoist.com/api/v1/) ≈ 67 rpm, but `/sync` batches up to **100 commands per request** → effective 6,700 ops/min — band 5.

data_portability.justification: Full API + `/sync` full-snapshot endpoint (100 full-sync req / 15 min).

sub_criteria.note: [Doist MCP server](https://github.com/Doist/todoist-ai) — hosted at `https://ai.todoist.net/mcp`, streamable HTTP, OAuth
Official MCP adoption + ecosystem directory listings

providers.bottom_line: Simple but well-rounded — Sync API batching rewards batch-capable clients, unified v1 fixed the move-task gotcha. Labels-only schema is the ceiling.
providers.gotcha: No `status` field beyond done/not-done; no start_date; no logged_hours

providers.name: Notion

sub_criteria.note: 11/14 native (priority, estimated_hours, logged_hours via custom properties)
Description as blocks is a real ops gap — no atomic "set description"
Rich-text is Notion blocks (proprietary recursive tree) — no standard Markdown surface

schema_flexibility.justification: 20+ [property types](https://developers.notion.com/reference/update-property-schema-object) — title, rich_text, number, select, multi_select, status, date, people, files, checkbox, url, email, phone, formula, relation, rollup, created_time, created_by, last_edited_time, last_edited_by, unique_id. No hard count cap.

rate_limits.justification: [~3 req/s per integration](https://developers.notion.com/reference/request-limits) (token bucket, bursts to 10) — ~180 rpm. No paid tier raises this.

real_time.justification: [Webhooks](https://developers.notion.com/reference/webhooks) shipped (2025+) — lightweight event notifications (re-fetch required). No user / workspace-membership events. Event coverage narrower than Jira / GitHub — band 3.

sub_criteria.note: Internal integration tokens (static bearer, single workspace)

data_portability.justification: API coverage is complete but [2025-09-03 "Data Source" split](https://developers.notion.com/docs/upgrade-guide-2025-09-03) was breaking; blocks-based export requires recursive fetching against 3 req/s rate; no dedicated bulk export.

sub_criteria.note: Notion AI readable via normal endpoints
No published major-host partnership cited at time of audit

providers.bottom_line: Notion's 2025 additions (webhooks + MCP + Agents) eliminated its catastrophic ratings. Block-based descriptions and rate limits remain the shape of its ceiling.
providers.gotcha: Description = recursive block tree at 3 req/s; 2025-09-03 Data Source split was breaking

providers.name: Trello

sub_criteria.note: 9/14 native — no priority, no estimated/logged_hours, `created_at` implicit in ObjectId only
No native subtasks — checklists only (checkItems are not cards; `convertToCardFromCheckItem` breaks parent link)
Ops gap: status = list position (fragile when users reorder lists)
Single REST `/1/` model (frozen for a decade)
No first-party SDK; community [`trello.js`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/trello.js) most actively maintained

schema_flexibility.justification: Native [custom fields](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/trello/rest/api-group-customfields/) — text, number, date, checkbox, list (dropdown). 5 types puts it in band 3.

rate_limits.formula: 100 req / 10 s per token × 60 s = 600 rpm
rate_limits.justification: [300 req / 10s per API key, 100 req / 10s per token](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/trello/guides/rest-api/rate-limits/) — binding = 600 rpm/token. > 200 429s per key → key-wide penalty.

real_time.justification: Model-scoped [webhooks](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/trello/guides/rest-api/webhooks/) — rich event list (createCard, updateCard, commentCard, addMemberToCard, updateCheckItem, createList, updateList, copyCard, voteOnCard, etc.) ≥ 30.

sub_criteria.note: OAuth 1.0a only — **no OAuth 2.0** on public REST

data_portability.justification: Full API + per-board JSON export (UI + API). Simple model = easy extraction.

sub_criteria.note: No Trello-specific MCP server (Atlassian Rovo / Remote MCP covers Jira/Confluence, not Trello)
No published partnerships for Trello specifically

providers.bottom_line: Trello is Atlassian's other task product — but nearly none of the Atlassian 2025/2026 AI investment reached it. Simple, stable, real-time solid; schema and AI are weak.
providers.gotcha: No subtasks, no priority, OAuth 1.0a only, no Trello-specific MCP

providers.name: MS Planner

sub_criteria.note: 9/14 native (no estimated/logged_hours; `percentComplete` limited to 0/50/100 — status is 3-state not 6-state)
No true subtasks (buckets are flat containers; checklist items don't nest)
Ops gap: premium / Project features API-inaccessible
Single Graph REST model (v1.0 stable + beta)
[Microsoft Graph SDKs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/sdks/sdks-overview) — first-party .NET, JS/TS, Java, Python, Go, PHP, PowerShell

schema_flexibility.justification: 6 boolean categories (v1.0) / 25 (beta) on `plannerAppliedCategories` — plan-level label descriptions, no typed custom fields.

rate_limits.formula: 130,000 req / 10 s × 60 s = 780,000 ops/min (per-tenant cap halved 2025-09-30)
rate_limits.justification: [130,000 req / 10s per app across tenants](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits) globally — generous in aggregate; [per-app/per-user-per-tenant cap was halved 2025-09-30](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling). [$batch](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/json-batching) allows 20 sub-requests.

real_time.justification: Graph [change notifications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/change-notifications-overview) support webhooks + Event Hubs + Event Grid — but **Planner resources are not in the supported-resources list**. Only [delta queries](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/delta-query-overview) apply — band 2.

sub_criteria.note: No self-serve token (Azure app registration required)

data_portability.justification: API coverage limited to basic plans — premium / Project plans inaccessible via Graph. Data locked in M365 ecosystem. No standalone export endpoint.

sub_criteria.note: Project Manager agent has no public developer API

providers.bottom_line: Planner is a narrow surface inside Graph. 2025 unification brought premium plans into the UI but not the API. Copilot Studio MCP support is the bright spot.
providers.gotcha: `percentComplete` is 0/50/100 only; Graph webhooks don't include Planner; premium plans API-inaccessible
